sentences.text: Pholidosaurus looked very much like a modern gharial and was roughly the same size.
The individual represented by the type mold was estimated to be around 25 cm in length.
An early description by Lydekker noted that the orbit was slightly smaller than the supratemporal fossa, the nasal bone reached the premaxilla, and the vomer appeared on the palate.
Fossils of Pholidosaurus have been found in northwestern Germany.
The type species, P. schaumburgensis, was named in 1841 from fossils found in the Wealden of Bückeburg, Germany.
The holotype is an almost complete skull named DORCM G97, which lacks the anterior part of the face.
The skull was found in Swanage or on the Isle of Purbeck, though the exact locality was not specified by the original author.

Barbini et al. (2026) reported evidence that the endocranial anatomy of P. purbeckensis is more similar to goniopholidids than dyrosaurids and found possible osteological correlates of nasal salt glands.
The genus Macrorhynchus is considered a junior synonym of Pholidosaurus.
Pholidosaurus is the type genus of the family Pholidosauridae.
Richard Lydekker classified Pholidosaurus in the family Goniopholididae in 1887 based on amphicoelous vertebrae and an orbit communicating with the lateral temporal fossa.
Buckley and Brochu (1999) concluded that Pholidosaurus formed a long-snouted clade that was the sister group to Crocodylia.
Pholidosaurus has recently been reassigned to the family Pholidosauridae, along with the genera Elosuchus, Sarcosuchus, and Terminonaris.
A 2002 study determined that Steneosaurus purbeckensis is the same species as Pholidosaurus decipiens, resulting in the combination Pholidosaurus purbeckensis.
Smith et al. (2016) suggested that Pholidosaurus purbeckensis is not closely related to the type species but is instead related to Fortignathus and Dyrosauridae.
Recent studies indicate that Thalattosuchia is a more basal lineage when dyrosaurids are excluded from the analysis.

Jouve et al. (2006) concluded that Pholidosaurus was a pholidosaurid, although in their phylogenetic analysis, thalattosuchians were included in the family, which could be considered paraphyletic without them.
Pholidosaurus lived during the Berriasian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
The genus lived from the Tithonian to the Aptian, between 149.2 and 113.2 million years ago.
